market_context: United States and general English-speaking market
title: Which berries have the most fiber?

seo.title: Berries with the most fiber: ranking per 100 g
seo.meta_description: Raspberries and blackberries contain much more fiber than blueberries and strawberries. Compare equal weights and a realistic 150 g serving.
seo.search_intent: Find which common berries contain the most fiber

excerpt: Among four common fresh berries, raspberries lead with about 6.5 g fiber per 100 g, followed by blackberries at 5.3 g. Blueberries and strawberries provide about 2.4 and 2.0 g respectively. A 150 g bowl of raspberries therefore approaches 9.8 g fiber.
content_html:
A mixed berry bowl looks like one nutritional category, but its fiber content can change dramatically depending on what fills the bowl. Raspberries and blackberries provide roughly two to three times as much fiber by weight as blueberries or strawberries.

For a fair ranking, the berries below are all raw and compared per 100 g.

BerryFiber per 100 gFiber per 150 g
Raspberries6.5 g~9.8 g
Blackberries5.3 g~8.0 g
Blueberries2.4 g~3.6 g
Strawberries2.0 g~3.0 g

The raspberry-strawberry gap is 4.5 g per 100 g. At a 150 g serving, that becomes nearly 7 g extra fiber—large enough to matter.

Why raspberries and blackberries rank high

Both are aggregate fruits made up of many small drupelets and edible seeds. That structure contributes a substantial amount of fibrous plant material.

This does not make blueberries or strawberries poor choices. They offer different vitamin and phytochemical profiles and still provide the water, fiber and volume of whole fruit.

A cup is not the same weight for every berry

Volume measures can blur the comparison because a cup of sliced strawberries does not weigh the same as a cup of raspberries. Per 100 g is useful for ranking; a realistic serving then shows what the difference means in the bowl.

What about frozen berries?

Unsweetened whole frozen berries keep the physical pulp and seeds, so their fiber remains largely intact. Jam and sweetened fruit spreads are different products because cooking, concentration and added sugar change the comparison.

If fiber is the specific goal, raspberries and blackberries have a clear advantage among these common berries. Variety still makes more sense than treating the ranking as a rule that excludes the others.

faq.question: Which common berry has the most fiber?
faq.answer: Raspberries among the four compared here, at about 6.5 g per 100 g.

faq.question: How much fiber is in blackberries?
faq.answer: About 5.3 g per 100 g, or roughly 8 g in a 150 g serving.

faq.question: Are blueberries high in fiber?
faq.answer: They provide about 2.4 g per 100 g—useful, but less than half the amount in raspberries.

faq.question: Does freezing berries remove fiber?
faq.answer: No. Whole unsweetened frozen fruit retains most fiber because fiber is part of the fruit's physical structure.
